title: Flatness detected on a complementary open and closed pair
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work either on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], or on the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with $j$ quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], inverse image $f^*=f^{-1}$ with the canonical constant-ring identifications [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], direct image $i_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and open extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Flat means that tensoring with the sheaf is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every $A_X$-module sheaf $H$,
$$H\text{ is flat}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j^*H\text{ and }i^*H\text{ are flat}.$$
In particular $j_!L$ is flat for every flat $A_U$-module sheaf $L$, and $i_*M$ is flat for every flat $A_Z$-module sheaf $M$. These assertions concern all ordinary module sheaves, without an étale-origin hypothesis on pro-étale sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), with the étale sequence in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open) and flatness as in sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3). Open/closed detection and preservation of flatness are extracted consequences of these sequences and the tensor-compatible exact inverse images, not literal assertions of the localization lemma.

proof.text: For etale sheaves use the geometric-fiber flatness criterion from WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.UpperLowerStar.FlatModuleCat. Every geometric point factors through exactly one member of the complementary pair. Pullback-fiber composition transports flatness. The open unit, closed counit and disjoint-range vanishing identities then give preservation by both extensions.

The intrinsic realization is an exact equivalence. Its right-tensor comparison transports exactness of right tensoring in both directions; braiding supplies left tensoring. Invariance of site flatness under isomorphism follows by transporting each local finite-relation factorization through the isomorphism. The canonical pullback and direct-image comparisons identify the constant-ring operations with transported fixed-scalar operations.

On fixed-scalar pro-etale module sheaves, inverse image preserves flatness. For the converse it suffices that right-exact tensorLeft H preserves monomorphisms. Its pullbacks are conjugate by the monoidal tensor isomorphism to tensoring by the flat pullbacks of H. Their kernels vanish. Exact inverse image identifies these kernels with restrictions of the original kernel, so complementary-pair zero detection proves the original kernel zero.

Apply the fixed-scalar detection result to open extension by zero and closed direct image. The open unit and closed counit identify the nonzero restrictions with the inputs; disjoint-range identities make the other restrictions zero. The zero sheaf is flat. Transfer back through the realization and the specified operation comparisons.

lean.statement: theorem openClosedFlatness_etale (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {X U Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsClosedImmersion i] (hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) (H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) : (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat H ↔ (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).obj H) ∧ CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj H))) ∧ (∀ L : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat L → CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat ((Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).obj L)) ∧ (∀ M : Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat M → CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat ((Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj M))
lean.note: Maintainer second-reader fix (NT-cc-Q60): both theorems parsed as `flat H ↔ ((restrictions flat) ∧ (∀ L, ...) ∧ (∀ M, ...))` because `↔` (precedence 20) binds looser than `∧` (35); the iff is now parenthesized so the statement is `(flat H ↔ restrictions flat) ∧ (j_! preserves flatness) ∧ (i_* preserves flatness)`, as in the node. The étale clauses use fixed-scalar sheaves `Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat A)`, the domain of the recorded Etale.upperStar/lowerStar/openImmersionLowerShriek, and `ObjectProperty.flat` there is tensor exactness for the project's global sheafified tensor `Etale.sheafMonoidalCategory`. That is the node's flatness (def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, Stacks 03ER(3)) for A_X-modules on this fixed-scalar model. The pro-étale clauses use the recorded SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.
